evals.prompt: Use the setup-github-labels skill to preview, and only preview, the label changes for github.com/example/app. Do not run any gh command that mutates; simulate the read-only ones. Assume `gh label list` returns exactly: `type: bug`, `type: feature`, `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `recommend-merge`, `needs-changes`, `dependencies`, `good first issue`. Assume neither `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` nor a `AGENTS.md` label pointer exists. Report the preview the skill would show the user.
evals.expected_output: A preview that buckets every manifest label into rename, update, or create, leaves non-manifest labels alone, and stops before applying.
expectations: `type: bug` and `type: feature` are listed as renames to `type:bug` and `type:feature`, not as new labels alongside the old ones.
`needs-changes` is listed as a rename to `recommend-revise`.
`dependencies` and `good first issue` are reported as untouched.
The contract file and the AGENTS.md pointer are both reported as to-be-created.
No `gh label create`, `gh label edit`, or `gh label delete` is executed, and the output asks the user to confirm before applying.

evals.prompt: The user has confirmed the preview and asks you to apply the setup-github-labels manifest to github.com/example/app, where `type: bug` currently exists and is on 141 issues. Do not actually run gh; instead print the exact shell you would run and explain, in two sentences, why the order matters. Then state what the skill's report step would say if every command succeeded.
evals.expected_output: A loop driven by labels.json that renames each `renamed_from` label with `gh label edit --name` before `gh label create --force`, preserving issue history, with no per-label hand-written commands.
expectations: The shell reads `labels.json` with jq rather than listing each label by hand.
For a label with `renamed_from`, `gh label edit <old> --name <new>` runs before `gh label create <new> --force`.
The explanation states that renaming keeps the 141 issues on the label whereas creating a new label would leave them on the old one.
The report distinguishes renamed, updated, and created labels.

evals.prompt: Using the setup-github-labels skill, write the updated `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` for a repository whose current file contains only a heading and this section, which must survive: `## Area labels\n\n`area:ui` and `area:cli` are applied by actions/labeler from path globs.` Also state the one-line change you would make to the root `AGENTS.md`, whose only relevant line currently reads `Triage uses the five standard labels. See docs/agents/triage-labels.md.`. Output the full new contract file and the AGENTS.md line.
evals.expected_output: A contract with a role table that has issue and PR columns, the rules from the skill, and the untouched area-labels section, plus a minimal AGENTS.md pointer.
expectations: The role table has one row per /triage role and separate columns for an issue label and a PR label.
`bug` maps to `type:bug` and `enhancement` maps to `type:feature`, with `type:task` named for maintenance, docs, or refactor work.
`needs-info` maps to `recommend-revise` on a PR, `ready-for-human` to `recommend-merge`, and `wontfix` to `recommend-close`.
The `## Area labels` section appears verbatim in the output.
The AGENTS.md change is a single pointer line that mentions PR verdicts and does not copy any table or rule.
